Ive played for 60 hours and would have played for more. After the recent update the game and/or its anti-cheat (rootkit?) cause my USB connections to randomly disconnect. This has affected my keyboard, mouse, wireless adapter and bluetooth adapter. 

Research indicate the issue is whatever they are doing cause the USB hardware to overheat. 

In either case, its now unplayable. As soon as I launch the game, every single time now, it causes my wireless network to drop. once im in an Operation my keyboard will all of a sudden stop responding to key presses. it will blink and the connection light will blink for a while. the more I play the worse it gets. Somtimes its the mouse thats affected and i cant turn or aim. Sometimes ive had the sound disconnect (via the bluetooth usb adapter). 

Im very leery of an asian made anti-cheat software. its always extremely intrusive and potentially dangerous. 

I cant say for sure they are doing anything nefarious, and until the last update i was willing to risk whatever they might be doing without my knowledge, but if their software makes my devices stop communicating with my computer then its time to uninstall. 

That said. its a fun... if brainless... game.

One of the worst games and most shameless cash grabs that I have EVER played.

Microtransactions: You cannot color base skins, INCLUDING the legendary Descendants that cost $50 or HUNDREDS of hours of play time to get. Colorable skins cost between 5 and 40 dollars but generally look WORSE than the base skin of that Descendant. You must buy new colors EVERY time you use them for 50 cents, and there's still NO black color. Battle pass does not include ANY Descendant skins until you get to level 50 and complete INSANE seasonal challenges, and over half of what is offered is just shaders, limited time boosts, and useless items that you can make for free in game but will never actually use. Every single aspect of the game has been fine tuned to increase grind and reduce enjoyment until you give up and just pay Nexon money.

Story: The combination of bad voice acting, terrible translations and sloppy writing was impossible to follow. Literally did not know what was happening or why I was shooting people for more than half of my playthrough. There are three magical McGuffins, a spirit guide that somehow knows even LESS than you do about said Mcguffins, and the bad guys are bad because... racism? Felt like either the devs paid someone on Fiver to write this or did it themselves.

Stability: I have a GTX 4070 Ti and even on High locked to 60 FPS I got frequent freezes and packet losses EVERY time large groups of enemies spawned, which happens a LOT.

Art Direction: The Descendants look like sexy sci fi adventurers, except when they are dressed as maids or dinosaurs. The guns, meanwhile, look like something out of Monster Hunter, with random organic bits tacked on, and the environments are poorly laid out with areas blatantly stolen from Warframe and Destiny 2. There is no cohesive vision and the skins make it even worse, leaving you wondering what the hell the intended genre was supposed to be. EVERY female character has the exact same 3D model, with identical standing, running and idle animations. The ONLY thing separating them is their clothes and hair. Even the reused Colossi assets were more varied.

Gameplay: Not bad but not great. Nothing to write home about, CERTAINLY not worth excusing the games other many faults. Most of the things you grind for like ultimate weapons and new Descendants ultimately feel like a huge waste of time, and you can just keep farming new weapon rolls so the crafting system really doesn't have any good use. You'll beat the game in like 20 hours, get a new descendant at 30 and then wonder what else there is to do. Nothing, that's what. And it's Nexon so you know it won't get any proper updates, they'll just move on to their next cash grab.

Invest your time in other, better free to play games.

In the current state of this game, honestly, just go play Warframe instead. 

This game is fun, at first, but VERY quickly becomes EXTREMELY repetitive. Also, I'm usually fine with grindy games, but oh my God, the amount of grinding needed in this game to acquire ANYTHING, ranging from new Descendants, to better weapons, to materials needed to get those better weapons, is asinine. There is a ten minute wait time to craft a single piece of material needed to upgrade a new weapon (a weapon that took 4 hours to research on its own BTW) so that it wasn't stuck at lvl 1 with a base DPS of 195. For comparison, at the level my character was at at the time, most of my weapons had a DPS stat of over 5,000, making the ultimate weapon that i'd crafted completely worthless unless I upgrade it. Ridiculous. There should not be this much waiting for something like a new weapon, imo.

Now for issues unrelated to gameplay itself... The script. Whoever is writing for this game, at least for its English translation, is either not actually fluent in English, or is working with an AWFUL script. So much of the dialogue comes across as stiff, unnatural, and sometimes straight up does not make sense. They also have a tendency to ramble and repeat things, over and over, while not actually explaining anything. I was paying attention to the dialogue and story for the first few hours, but gave up because listening to the droning dialogue became a chore. The lip-sync also more often than not doesn't match what is being said, like, at all.

TL;DR: Just play Warframe for now.

Free to download, not free to play. This game is a dream come true for looter shooter fans who have been waiting for a game like this. As a fan of Destiny and Division, I longed for a game with endgame progression and elusive lore that would keep me grinding even after completion.

This game delivers exactly that, but be warned.

This game exemplifies the direction of the gaming industry. It features a monetised shop, making it effectively "pay to progress." Beyond the usual cosmetic items, there are items designed to psychologically encourage players to spend money to advance. This dark system preys on those with addictive tendencies, making the grind seem insurmountable without spending.

This is the troubling future of gaming. If you are up for the grind, you can achieve it. However, it will take around 200 hours to unlock the ultimate descendants legitimately.

Good luck!

[h1] The Best Review for The First Descendant [/h1]
Absolutely incredible game. It is sad that this is the only game that has been released in the past 2 years that I have actually enjoyed. It is a great game if you enjoy Loot and Shooters, Open World Games, and / or MMO games. If you like RPG games as well, this might also be a good game to try out.

[h2] Storyline and Gameplay [/h2]

The storyline is decent, but I haven't paid that much attention - I just like the battles.
The music is absolutely amazing. It sounds just amazing - the strings, vocals and violin go so well together and this game's soundtrack really showcases this. 

The grind to get characters can definitely be challenging, and I am trying to currently get Ultimate Bunny without buying them. I am currently just trying to unlock all locations in the map to be able to get the correct amount of components for them, but the game itself is actually really fun.


[h2] Suggestions and more [/h2]

One thing that I would like to see implemented though, is a way to remove worse, duplicated items from your inventory. For example, if you have an weapon that is a higher level then if there are duplicates of that weapon that are a lower level, then the lower level duplicates should be able to be destroyed for parts.

Anyway, I was an early access / beta player, and it is good to see the game in it's current state. There currently doesn't seem to be any bugs that I have noticed or at least any bugs that I remember, and that is incredible for a game made in the 2020s.

This studio actually seems to care about the game, and I hope it stays around for a long time. This game could make more game studios realise that a game can be successful if it is developed for a long time, and show that the player-base doesn't mind if the game takes longer to develop if the game is significantly better after the waiting time.

The beta was around 1 year ago just for reference.

They seem to of spent 1 year finishing the final bits of the game from the look of it, and the work really shows.


[h2] Graphics and Performance [/h2]

Graphics are amazing in this game due to Unreal Engine 5's Nanite and Lumen graphical features.

Performance is a bit bad, but I am sure this will get better with time. I have a Ryzen 5 5600x, 16GB DDR4 Ram and a RTX 2070 Super 8GB and it gets around 70fps @ 1080p Medium-High settings, This is with DLSS Quality mode enabled.


[h2] Summary [/h2]

Genuinely, one of the best games I have played in a while. I genuinely believe that this game goes far, and that Nexon Studios actually keeps the game alive for a while.

This game is going to be big, I can already tell.

Anyway - great game, highly recommend. 10/10

I wanted to give this a fair shot before posting a review, but after 90 hours I honestly can't take it anymore. The game needs serious optimization. I've fallen through the map multiple times just queuing into missions and have been stuck in so many glitches I've lost count. We can borrow modding systems and the works from other games but couldn't be bothered to code in an unstuck feature. Plus the shader loader. I'm hearing people are cooking their CPUS to play this game and not even in high or ultra. Not to mention every time they patch something it resets your settings entirely. Missions bug out and do not drop anything at all frequently. The teleportation when in parties needs to be fixed specifically on infiltration. There should be no reason if a party is doing a mission together within 5 feet of each other that they all need to be teleported on top of each other, and in a stealth mission nonetheless. 

The game is about as good as you'd expect any looter shooter being pumped out in 2024 is. You can farm everything except for cosmetics but the grind is lengthy and quite honestly the worst snooze fest I've ever had the displeasure of taking part in and I've spent 1000 hours watching Sims roam around a dollhouse for funsies. 

The characters need balancing as well. You get 14 if you count the ultimates as different characters, personally I wouldn't, it's like getting a prime Warframe but with more bits everywhere. The game relies heavily on that "aesthetic" to capture their audience otherwise the story you can skip through, I've seen better writing from a third grade class, voice acting (except for the Korean audio) is like watching an English movie with a Spanish voice over. The best thing about the game is probably the grapple and even that is subpar. It works when it wants to, just like jumping works when it wants to and it's far too short in my personal opinion. Think Overwatch Widowmaker with like 1/4 of the range. Game is fun for maybe an additional 20 hours give or take after the story but after that it really just falls flat. The characters and guns are the only incentive since you can't grind for cosmetics which is pretty lame for an rpg. 

There's no trade system which is also a huge let down. I have duplicates of codes that can't be used or broken down so they are just eating inventory space. I wanted to be fair but given the company's reputation and the quality of the game they put out, even if it's free, just isn't there. Especially when you think of all the games they siphoned from to make TFD. The math isn't mathing. I've seen better drops from indie developers and yes they love their games but if a developer doesn't love the work they are putting out then they are just looking for a buncha little dummies to spend on their cash cow and that's not something I can get behind. It's beyond grimey. 

However, if you need help getting a good nights rest then this game is a 10/10.

Wow uh, this is garbage. (TLDR: 2/10)

Graphics:
I feel as if modern gaming believes that visual clarity and graphical detail should require your PC to be so beefy that it'll make NASA blush from the specs it'll need. Seriously though, this game does an awful job with optimizing and using its textures in a way to make memorable areas. They look pretty, sure, but they lack an artist tinge or care that makes everything populating the game feel inconsistant.

Gameplay:
This strongly feels like developers took a look at looter shooters like Destiny and Warframe and superficially took the mechanics from either without much thought or care. It's technically slightly faster than Destiny and shares the 4 abilities with a energy pool like Warframe. Difference is, the creativity of each ability and level design is simply woeful garbage, refusing to take advantage of it's mobility save for the one hallway transition that no one cares about. Abilities in this game feel lackluster, confusing all the pretty effects used for them fall flat from how they work, their lack of audio design, and how no one wants you to use your abilities in a creative manner. 
This is further punctured by the grappling hook, which feels fun for 2 minutes and then you realize that it's the most unsatisfiying mobility tool I've used in a while. The inertia feels kneejerk at best and counterintuitive at worse, coupled with the in-game areas rarely ever give you a chance to really flex your mobility beyond getting up somewhere.
Gunplay is painfully okay, sounds work and I guess you'll have fun. But any punch or satisfaction in these weapons are non-existent and remind me of when I tried playing Outriders again. Couple this with a stingy ammo economy and I ended up really hating it. Specficially because the game lets you equip 3 weapons, even those under the same ammo type. However, the game doesn't seperate the ammo counts on those of the same type, which ends up defeating the potenial freedom the game could've had. Generic at best and completely shafting the shotgun or any interesting weapon combinations.
Finally is that forgettable enemy design, it feels like what Destiny 2 haters feel when they're describing the enemy design. Mind you, I'm not talking about enemy appearence, because I honestly find them mega mucking forgetable, they're outright stupid and only serve to act as pushovers for this lackluster power fantasy.

The Crafting:
This is literally the embodiment of "we have Destiny 2/Warframe at home" except they straight up lie to the player at point. The way you upgrade and craft things is directly lifted Warframe, down to how you mod your weapons or how it'll take forever to make something new. Difference is, someone must've thought Destiny 2 had some good ideas and made it so it's a chore to even upgrade your weapons. Hell, you even get new Warfr- sorry, "Descendants" from farming a single boss with a stupid name and waiting for a day.

Cash Shop:
No, just- god no don't even pay for the hot trash in this game. If I wanted to throw money at a company I'd actually swallow my pride and play Genshin Impact or something. Gods sake, if you wanna play a free-2-play looter shooter Warfame and Destiny 2 are LITERALLY RIGHT THERE. Go spend your money somewhere else.

Ive got 58 hours into this game so far, just finished the main story, and there's definitely a lot of issues here. The grappling hook is frustrating to use, when running around your guy doesnt always step up over little rocks and whatnot and gets stuck, you CONSTANTLY get crit right off the bat in a fight causing your shield to vanish and be completely useless, in game chat is one of the worst implementations i've ever seen (its never showing unless you look, so you never see new messages), the in game shop is EXPENSIVE! Its a free game so im totally for the shop but the prices are absolute insanity! I think the amount of parts you need to farm everything should be cut by at least 25% because its soooooo tedius and NOT fun!

Then one of the things i hate the most... Near the end of the game, the difficulty seems to go from easy to super hard going from 1 mission to the next, and its insane! This happens multiple times and now that i've completed the missions, i can tell its just certain missions where they overwhelm you with the amount of enemies. Its definitely designed so that you should always go in with 2 or more people, otherwise you may find yourself getting incredibly frustrated. People need to stop saying the game is soloable! I play Ajax so i'm mostly stuck fighting 1 target at a time so maybe thats my issue there? Hard to say until i play other descendants.

Another large issue is word choice through out the game... Some stats show a positive number and they mean negative, and sometimes positive... And some are negative and different ones mean a positive change and others a negative, so its really complicated to figure things out. There's a lot of other strage words and meanings that are clearly translated terribly. This means understanding the game, mods, and builds can be extremely difficult.

On a positive note, the game play is fun when everything works right, the customization is awesome (although there's some things that could change, like let us level up the reactors and components!), the graphics on the descendants are great and most of the scenery is too, i like the abilities and the different playstyles of the descendants, and all that greats some great replay value.
